_note: Emergency decision tree: a crewmate collapses or feels unwell. Collapse and chest pain have their own branches; anything else goes to a general branch that measures, records and escalates, without trying to diagnose. Each step is labelled 'Published' (wording checked against an opened publication, cited in source) or 'Demo copy' (team wording, not a protocol). tests/emergency.test.ts checks every link, label and source. No medication or dosing advice anywhere.
limitsNote: Hinkelbein et al. 2020 covers weightlessness only. CPR has never been performed on a human in spaceflight.

steps.text: Is the crewmember conscious and responsive to voice?
steps.hint: Say their name, tap the shoulder. Ten seconds, no longer.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Mockup cites Hinkelbein et al. 2020 (not yet opened by the team).

steps.text: Is the main problem chest pain?
steps.hint: Ask them what is wrong. If they cannot say, or you are not sure, answer NO.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Routes to the chest-pain branch or the general branch. Not from a published protocol.

steps.text: Are they breathing regularly, not just gasping?
steps.hint: Look, listen and feel for no more than ten seconds. Occasional gasps do not count as breathing.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Mockup cites Hinkelbein et al. 2020 (not yet opened by the team).

steps.text: Restrain them, keep the airway open, attach the monitor and stay with them
steps.hint: Call the crew medical officer now. If breathing stops, go back one step and answer NO.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Not from a published protocol.

steps.text: Start chest compressions now and call for the defibrillator
steps.hint: Use the Evetts-Russomano method first. If you cannot compress well with it, switch to the Reverse-Bear-Hug method. Once they are restrained on the crew medical restraint system, use the Handstand method if the spacecraft's size allows it. Rate, depth and breaths are the same as in your Earth-based CPR training. Use the defibrillator only once they are restrained on an electrically isolated surface.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Hinkelbein et al. 2020, Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y), Recommendations 2, 3 and 10. The guideline gives no compression rate, depth or ratio of its own and refers to the Earth-based AHA/ERC guidelines, so no numbers are shown. Stays Demo copy until a team member has opened the paper.

steps.text: Is the pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back, or are they short of breath?
steps.hint: Ask them to point to where it hurts. Watch the breathing while they answer.
steps.logYes: Spreading pain or short of breath
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. The CPR guideline does not cover a conscious crewmember with chest pain.

steps.text: Keep them at rest and restrained, attach the monitor and call the crew medical officer now
steps.hint: Do not give any medication from this screen. If they stop responding, restart from step 1.
steps.logYes: At rest, monitor on, medical officer called
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Not from a published protocol.

steps.text: Keep them at rest, attach the monitor and recheck every five minutes
steps.hint: If the pain spreads, breathing changes or they stop responding, restart from step 1.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Not from a published protocol.

steps.text: Read their vitals and note what they describe
steps.hint: Heart rate, blood pressure, temperature and glucose if you can. The panel on the right shows their latest stored readings. Write down where it hurts and when it started.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. General steps (measure, record, escalate) for problems outside the collapse and chest-pain branches. Not from a published protocol and not a diagnosis.

steps.text: Are any readings red, or are they getting worse?
steps.hint: Red means a reading crossed a critical limit. Worse means pain, breathing or alertness changing for the worse.
steps.logNo: No red reading, not getting worse
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. General steps (measure, record, escalate) for problems outside the collapse and chest-pain branches. Not from a published protocol and not a diagnosis.

steps.text: Keep them at rest, call the crew medical officer now and stay with them
steps.hint: Send the step log and their latest readings to the ground. If they stop responding, restart from step 1.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. General steps (measure, record, escalate) for problems outside the collapse and chest-pain branches. Not from a published protocol and not a diagnosis.

steps.text: Keep them at rest and recheck their vitals in five minutes
steps.hint: Tell the crew medical officer. If anything gets worse or they stop responding, restart from step 1.
steps.logYes: At rest, recheck in five minutes
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. General steps (measure, record, escalate) for problems outside the collapse and chest-pain branches. Not from a published protocol and not a diagnosis.
